$comment: Single source of truth for the companion-plugin packaging pipeline.
and the staged tree cannot disagree.
Every plugin is staged into <stageRoot>/<id>/, every sub-option into
<stageRoot>/<id>__<subId>/. The wizard installs exactly those two folder
shapes, which is why payload entries describe what goes inside them.
payload:  copied from the plugin submodule at build time (repo content)
artifacts: copied from that plugin's own build output (compiled files)
dest '.':  the source is a directory and its CONTENTS land in the root
A payload source beginning with ../ is repo-relative rather than
submodule-relative, for files this repository owns because it cannot push
to the plugin repositories. A file that upstream produces outside CMake
belongs in payload too, not artifacts: CI builds every plugin through
CMake alone, so anything their own build script generates is never built.
The upstream fomod/ModuleConfig.xml files are NOT reused: IEDSyncTogether's
copy references a '00 Core' folder its own build script never creates, so it
is stale. STN owns the one wizard and this manifest is the only source.

plugins.rationale: Transport every companion plugin links against. Installed whenever any companion plugin is selected.
plugins.payloadNote: The ini is owned by this repository rather than by the submodule: the plugin repositories are pinned and this project does not push to them, so an edit inside one would never reach CI or a release. It also must not live under GameFiles/Skyrim, because two workflows copy that tree wholesale into the always-installed core - which would install an ini for a DLL the user may not have chosen.

plugins.artifactsNote: OSKSE.pex and OStimTogetherNative.pex are compiled by compat/OStimUIConsent/compile-ui-consent.ps1, which needs PapyrusCompiler.exe from an installed Skyrim. A CI runner has no Skyrim, so those two scripts are not packaged here; OStimTogether's own release script builds them on a machine that does. The wizard description states the consequence.

plugins.payloadNote: The esp is owned by this repository, like STRPluginMessagingAPI's ini and for the same reason. Upstream generates it in build-vortex.ps1 - Write-MinimalPlugin writes a TES4 header plus CNAM and SNAM subrecords - rather than in CMake. CI builds every plugin through CMake alone, so that script never runs and no esp is produced; listing this as an artifact therefore made the package unbuildable, because the staging step demanded a file nothing in the pipeline could create. The committed copy is byte-identical to the script's output (110 bytes, sha256 9811c7bd...), and it is only that script's output: if upstream ever changes the generator, this file has to be regenerated by hand, which is what the hash above is for. The esp is a marker the plugin resolves by name - IEDBridge and RemoteIEDRenderer both pass it as the plugin key to IED's Papyrus calls - so it has to exist for the plugin to work at all.
